newsitem.title: USA: Peace process can survive housing dispute - U.S..
newsitem.headline: Peace process can survive housing dispute - U.S..

text.p: The Middle East peace process can survive this week's scheduled ground-breaking for a controversial Jewish housing project in predominantly Arab East Jerusalem, the U.S. State Department said on Monday.

"It can survive the ground-breaking," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said at a briefing, referring to the peace process. But he stressed that the United States still did not support the Israeli housing project.
"The United States has not changed its position on the Israeli construction proposal at Har Homa, or Jabal Abu Ghneim, what the Arabs call Jabal Abu Ghneim," Burns said.

President Bill Clinton has said the project "builds mistrust." Others in the U.S. government, including Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, have pressed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel the plan, Burns said.

"Now it appears that the Israeli government is determined to move forward...And we just hope that, in working out the obvious differences on this issue between the Israelis and Palestinians...that any difference of opinion on this be pursued in a non-violent way," Burns said.
In addition, he said, the United States hoped that Israelis and Palestinians would "continue to talk together, sit down politically and try to negotiate their differences."
